name: Ibuprofen
executiveSummary: NSAID analgesic/antipyretic. Adult PO: **200–400 mg every 6–8 h** (self-care max **1.2 g/day**). Pediatric PO: **5–10 mg/kg every 6–8 h** (max **30 mg/kg/day**). IV (pain/fever): adult **400–800 mg every 6 h**; pediatrics **5–10 mg/kg every 6–8 h**.
indications:
## Indications

- Fever and mild–moderate pain (PO first-line with paracetamol).
- Musculoskeletal inflammatory conditions / JIA (PO regimens).
- IV when PO not possible (post-op, inpatient) — specific products.

## Precautions

- Avoid in active ulcer/GI bleed, severe renal/hepatic failure, 3rd trimester, NSAID/ASA allergy.
- Renal risk with dehydration; caution with ACEI/ARB, diuretics, anticoagulants.
- **IV ≠ PO**. Neonatal PDA IV is a different regimen.

> Calculate pediatrics by **weight**. Check suspension mg/mL.

adulto.presentation: PO: tabs/caps 200–400–600 mg; suspension 20–40 mg/mL. IV: vial per brand.
adulto.dose: **PO** fever/pain: **200–400 mg every 6–8 h** (usual short-course max **1.2 g/day**; supervised inflammation up to **2.4–3.2 g/day**). **IV** pain/fever: **400–800 mg every 6 h** (usual max **3.2 g/day**); infuse ≥30 min.
adulto.administration: PO with food if GI upset. IV: dilute per label; no rapid bolus.

pediatrico.presentation: Suspension 20 or 40 mg/mL; pediatric tabs. Hospital IV per product.
pediatrico.dose: **PO**: **5–10 mg/kg/dose every 6–8 h**; max **30 mg/kg/day**. JIA: **20–40 mg/kg/day** PO divided (specialist). **IV**: **5–10 mg/kg every 6–8 h** (max **30 mg/kg/day**).
pediatrico.administration: PO with oral syringe; shake. IV per label.
pediatrico.notes: Confirm 20 vs 40 mg/mL. Avoid <3 months unless labeled.

neonatal.presentation: IV for PDA (e.g. Pedea) ≠ oral antipyretic.
neonatal.dose: Not routine oral antipyretic. PDA: NNU regimen only.
neonatal.notes: Do not interchange mL with oral suspension.

stability:
## Stability

- Oral suspension: room temp per label; shake. Diluted IV: per product insert.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Dyspepsia, nausea, epigastric pain; ulcer/GI bleed; fluid retention; ↑ creatinine; bronchospasm; rash. IV: phlebitis, hypotension if rapid.
